goal: semantic parity (NOT performance) between rayx lane_impl='std' (std::thread ServiceLane) and lane_impl='hpx' (cooperative HpxLane): both honor the same RayX lane contract
machine: macOS laptop, 10 cores (4 P + 6 E), single locality

scenarios.basic: round-robin burst via get(): all complete, one row each, prefix + lane balance
scenarios.wait: wait(num_returns=1) partitions ready/rest, non-consuming, all retire
scenarios.as_completed: as_completed yields each future once, all complete
scenarios.chunked: chunked service completes, echoes chunks/chunk_delay_ms, full run
scenarios.queued_cancel: victim queued behind a spin occupier -> cancel True, status=cancelled, chunks_completed == 0
scenarios.running_cancel: started chunked request -> cancel True, status=cancelled, 0 < chunks_completed < chunks
scenarios.bounded_admission: cap full -> QueueFullError (no-op on depth); admitted + occupier complete
scenarios.lane_stats: shape {actor_id,queue_depth,active}; active+depth under load; returns to idle after drain

note: Parity/semantics only; timing is an observation, NEVER a gate; no speedup claim and no 'HPX beats Ray' claim. This is the opt-in rayx HpxLane serialized backend (lane_impl='hpx'), NOT the experiment-20 hpx::async / hpx::dataflow task-pool probe. Not Ray Serve, not a Ray object store, not real inference. No analyzer / benchmark-JSONL-schema / driver / CI / Future-ownership change; no HPX internals exposed. Raw per-backend JSON is experiment-local scratch under results/ (gitignored), NOT the v1 benchmark schema.
